title.en: Create and import your own module

say.en: Need a square root, a random dice roll or an average? Python already ships these in its standard library. We just have to know where to look. In this lesson: Use built-in functions.
Import math, random and statistics.
Create and import your own module.

body.en: *Built-in functions* are always available without importing anything, for example input(), print(), int(), float(), len(), abs(), max(), min(), round(), pow(), sum() and type().
body.kn: ಬಿಲ್ಟ್-ಇನ್ ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ಗಳು ಯಾವುದನ್ನೂ ಇಂಪೋರ್ಟ್ ಮಾಡದೆ ಸದಾ ಲಭ್ಯ: input(), print(), int(), len(), abs(), max(), min(), round() ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ.

title.en: On the board: Using the math, random and statistics modules

say.en: import math loads the whole module, so we write the module name with a dot.
from math import sqrt loads just that function, and we call it directly.
Here are some results. ceil rounds up, floor rounds down, and pow and sqrt give floats.
random.randint of 1 and 6 gives a whole number from 1 to 6, both ends included, like a die.
statistics.mean of 2, 4 and 9 is 5.

prompt.en: Sort each function: built-in (no import), or from the math, random or statistics module.
prompt.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್ ಅಂತರ್ನಿರ್ಮಿತವೇ ಅಥವಾ math, random, statistics ಮಾಡ್ಯೂಲ್‌ನದೇ ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಿ.

explanation.en: Built-in functions are always available. sqrt, ceil and floor need import math; randint, randrange and random need import random; mean, median and mode need import statistics.
explanation.kn: ಅಂತರ್ನಿರ್ಮಿತ ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ಗಳು ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ಲಭ್ಯ. ಉಳಿದವಕ್ಕೆ import math, import random, import statistics ಬೇಕು.

say.en: Where does it come from? Sort each function: built-in no import, or from the math, random or statistics module.
say.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್ ಅಂತರ್ನಿರ್ಮಿತವೇ ಅಥವಾ math, random, statistics ಮಾಡ್ಯೂಲ್‌ನದೇ ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಿ.

body.en: A module is a .py file containing functions and variables. import math loads the whole module and we write math.sqrt(16). from math import sqrt loads only sqrt and we write sqrt(16). Useful *modules* are math (sqrt, ceil, floor, pow, pi), random (random, randint, randrange) and statistics (mean, median, mode). Any program saved as a .py file can be imported as a user-defined module.
body.kn: ಮಾಡ್ಯೂಲ್ ಎಂದರೆ ಫಂಕ್ಷನ್‌ಗಳಿರುವ .py ಫೈಲ್. import math ಎಂದರೆ ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ಮಾಡ್ಯೂಲ್; math.sqrt(16) ಎಂದು ಬರೆಯುತ್ತೇವೆ. from math import sqrt ಎಂದರೆ sqrt ಮಾತ್ರ. math, random, statistics ಉಪಯುಕ್ತ ಮಾಡ್ಯೂಲ್‌ಗಳು.

tagline.en: Mixed board-style questions on modules: import forms, math outputs and types, random possible-output questions and statistics programs.

myth.en: from random import randint then calling random.randint(1, 6) works.

truth.en: With from random import randint, call randint(1, 6). The name random itself was never imported, so random.randint is a NameError. The from form brings in only the listed names. Mixing the two styles is a very common error-spotting question.

say.en: Built-in functions (len, abs, round, pow) need no import.
from m import f → call f(), not m.f().
fabs, pow and sqrt give floats; ceil and floor give ints.
Random programs give different outputs; reason with ranges.

goal.en: Mixed board-style questions on modules: import forms, math outputs and types, random possible-output questions and statistics programs.

task.en: Which module does each name come from?

explain.en: math holds constants, rounding, powers and trigonometry; random holds random number tools; statistics holds mean, median and mode.

takeaway.en: Built-in functions (len, abs, round, pow) need no import.

narration.en: Many people think: from random import randint then calling random.randint(1, 6) works. Actually: With from random import randint, call randint(1, 6). The name random itself was never imported, so random.randint is a NameError. The from form brings in only the listed names. Mixing the two styles is a very common error-spotting question.

problem.en: Use the math and statistics modules to process the marks 45, 78, 62 and 78.

narration.en: Let us trace this code together. Use the math and statistics modules to process the marks 45, 78, 62 and 78. Predict the output before we run it.

say.en: Let us trace this code together. Use the math and statistics modules to process the marks 45, 78, 62 and 78. Predict the output before we run it.
import math.
import statistics.
print(statistics.meanmarks).
print(statistics.modemarks).
print(math.ceil65.75).
mean equals (45 plus 78 plus 62 plus 78) / 4 equals 65.75; mode equals 78 it appears twice; ceil65.75 equals 66.

So the answer is 65.75
78
66.
